story.title: India's Draft IT Rules Draw Criticism for Expanding Content Blocking Powers With No Transparency Safeguards
story.summary: The Hindu's editorial analysis of India's draft amendments to the Information Technology Rules warns that proposed changes represent a significant tightening of state control over the digital public sphere, departing from existing judicial rulings on free expression. The draft rules would expand the government's ability to block online content — including AI-generated material — without adequate transparency requirements, due process, or independent review mechanisms. Legal experts cited in the piece argue that the amendments risk enabling digital overreach at a scale that could chill legitimate speech for millions of internet users in India.
